components.gap: Narrowed source variant. Durrett (p. 244) defines uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of random variables and then derives sup E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity, so integrability and L1-boundedness are consequences of the definition. Body 17 defines the notion only for families of real integrable random variables, so the source form (a property of arbitrary families that forces integrability) is not preserved; it is also the form the source's Theorem 4.6.2 uses (see C003).

components.gap: Unstated assumption (adaptedness). The route's definition def:p15-filtration-martingale (handbook/parts/p15/martingales-and-convergence.tex 18-26) defines adaptedness but does not require it of martingales, submartingales or supermartingales, and this chapter never states it; the convention that processes are adapted appears only later on the route, in def:p15-os-conventions (handbook/parts/p15/optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 11-13). (a) Annex 204-206 infers that the finite-limit event and the limsup/liminf are F_infinity-measurable from the measurability of the X_n; without X_n being F_n-measurable this does not give the F_infinity-measurable choice of X_infinity asserted at body 114-116. (b) Annex 219-221 uses the F_n-events where the bracket E(X_infinity|F_n) - X_n is at most -1/k; these are F_n-events only if X_n is F_n-measurable, so the written proof of X_n <= E(X_infinity|F_n) (body 117-120) rests on the unstated hypothesis. The equivalence of the three convergence conditions and the sign change are otherwise written. Durrett's Theorem 4.6.4 concerns submartingales in his sense, whose definition (p. 217) includes adaptedness as condition (ii).

components.gap: (1) Unstated assumption (adaptedness). Annex 234-235 says X_n is F_n-measurable in order to make it a version of E(X_infinity|F_n). The route's definition def:p15-filtration-martingale (handbook/parts/p15/martingales-and-convergence.tex 18-26) defines adaptedness but does not require it of martingales, submartingales or supermartingales, and this chapter never states it; the convention that processes are adapted appears only later on the route, in def:p15-os-conventions (handbook/parts/p15/optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 11-13). The martingale identity gives only almost-sure equality with an F_n-measurable variable, and no completeness of a sub-sigma-algebra is assumed (body 32-33). Annex 239-240 then relies on the F_infinity-measurable limit version constructed in the proof of thm:p15-submartingale-ui, which needs the same hypothesis (see C007). Durrett's martingales are adapted by definition (p. 217, condition (ii)). (2) Source locator. The identification X_infinity = E(Z|F_infinity) (body 140-141) is placed under the citation of lems. 4.6.5-6 and thm. 4.6.7 (body 142). Those items (pp. 246-247) do not contain it; in the source it is the identification step in the proof of Theorem 4.6.8 (p. 247).

components.gap: Omitted source claims in the cited continuation of Theorem 4.6.9 (pp. 247-248). Durrett borrows a line from K. L. Chung inviting the reader to judge whether the theorem is obvious or incredible, argues both readings, the 'obvious' one (the best guess of 1_A from growing information should approach 1_A) and the 'incredible' one (Kolmogorov's 0-1 law), and then judges that, together with later applications, the theorem is very useful even if the argument does not make it literally incredible. The entry (body 161-176, annex 287-305) gives the statement, the almost-sure and L1 limit and the Kolmogorov 0-1 proof only. The Chung attribution, the two-readings discussion and the evaluative claim are absent.

components.gap: Omitted source definitions and interpretation. components.gap: Omitted justificatory claim.
